prep.summary:
Invoice pagination, summary-performance, and PDF credit-rendering work is complete and validated. Pagination now has bounded API/service behavior and comprehensive tests. Invoice-summary aggregation was moved outside currency loops and uses batched minor-unit conversion, reducing tenant 73 from about 2,417 queries/39 seconds to 37 queries/4.3 seconds while preserving all 14,802 values; a stable query-count regression test was added.

PDF credit lines now preserve negative amounts, appear directly after related items, and use the shared locale-aware `format_money()` formatter, with exact positive, negative, and zero-format tests. PDF table layout was also corrected by centralizing points-to-page-height conversion and reserving table headers once per document. An 86-item invoice regression initially produced three pages, then passed after the fix. The full invoice PDF suite passed with 14 tests and one skip; golden files remained byte-stable; the broader billing suite passed with 83 tests and four skips. Ruff checks and formatting also passed.

The final diff contains four changed files with 217 insertions and 184 deletions, and `git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors. The immediate next step is visually comparing the three generated PDFs to confirm the corrected pagination and credit/refund layout.

Broader follow-up remains: explicitly validate March 2025 payroll taxes, filing totals, and reconciliation despite review approval; investigate the separate credit-after-refund discrepancy ($87.50 expected versus $90.00 received); and consider project-wide formatting and typing, wider tests, legacy CSV deprecation, and partial-refund documentation. Use `python:3.12.9-slim` and consult before changing the CI matrix.
